verdict.root_cause: cartservice requests are slow because every Redis cache round trip carries a fixed ~300ms of added delay. Sampled traces around the alert show each HGET and HMSET span costing ~300-313ms of self-time while cartservice's own gRPC handlers contribute sub-millisecond self-time, with identical cost for reads and writes and near-constant magnitude across traces — the signature of a fixed per-round-trip delay rather than load-proportional queuing [tr_516df667b488]. The change log describes exactly that mechanism: a recurring platform-automation cycle that attaches a traffic-shaping sidecar injecting a fixed 300ms egress delay into the cart-service network namespace [tr_33f3a8e5e4c4]. The change record claims removal ~1.6h before onset, but the 300ms penalty is still present at 02:27, so either the removal did not take effect on the running instance or the untrusted change log is incomplete near onset. The delay compounds at the edge (AddItem makes two sequential cache calls, then frontend issues a GetCart, yielding ~900ms user-facing POSTs) [tr_516df667b488], which explains why frontend, checkoutservice and loadgenerator alerted seconds after cartservice and why checkoutservice went from a flat-zero baseline to ~1.1% mean / 6.9% peak errors with a change point at 02:12 [tr_19bf7a508e5a]. cartservice itself is healthy, logging cart operations through the end of the window with no errors or restarts [tr_a709aa66d542].
verdict.reasoning: The only measured anomaly with a located mechanism is latency in cartservice's Redis hop [tr_516df667b488], and its shape settles the mechanism: uniform across reads and writes, near-constant magnitude, concentrated entirely in child cache spans. That excludes cartservice logic, other downstreams, write-path contention and frontend slowness, and also argues against genuine Redis load, which would be variable and load-proportional. A fixed additive per-round-trip delay matches the documented 300ms traffic-shaping sidecar on the cart-service namespace [tr_33f3a8e5e4c4]. The class is dependency_latency, not bad_config: requests still succeed and the failure is the wait itself; no wrong address, port or artifact is in effect. cartservice is blamed over checkoutservice or frontend because the callers' symptoms follow arithmetically from a 300ms-per-cache-call cart path [tr_19bf7a508e5a], while the reverse does not. Fix is to detach the shaping sidecar and verify the revert landed on the running instance.
open_questions: Is the traffic-shaping sidecar still attached to the running cart-service namespace? The change log's claimed removal contradicts the live 300ms trace signature and was never checked directly.
When did the Redis delay actually begin? All sampled traces cluster in the final ~60s of a two-hour window, so onset cannot be aligned with 02:12 or 02:26:45.
Are checkoutservice's errors cart-path timeouts? The metric groups only by service_name with no downstream target dimension [tr_19bf7a508e5a], and redis-cart was never queried directly.

alternatives.root_cause: The redis-cart backend itself became slow (server-side stall or network path degradation) independent of any injected delay.
alternatives.why_not: Redis was never queried directly, but a real server-side stall would produce variable, load-proportional, read/write-asymmetric latency; the observed cost is near-constant and identical for HGET and HMSET [tr_516df667b488], which fits an injected fixed delay and matches a documented 300ms shaping sidecar [tr_33f3a8e5e4c4].

alternatives.root_cause: A REDIS_ADDR override pointed cartservice at a wrong host/port, forcing a slower or mis-resolved cache path.
alternatives.why_not: A wrong address would typically yield connection errors or resolution failures, yet cart operations complete normally with no connection errors [tr_a709aa66d542]; the override was also reverted ~1.3h before onset [tr_33f3a8e5e4c4], and a uniform 300ms penalty is not what an address change produces.

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating the container gives cartservice a fresh network namespace, dropping any traffic-shaping egress rule still attached to the live instance. Within a few minutes: Redis HGET/HMSET child spans should fall from ~300-313ms self-time to single-digit ms, frontend GET traces from ~301ms to <50ms and AddItem POSTs from ~900ms to <100ms; cartservice logs should resume their steady cart-operation cadence.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if post-restart traces still show ~300ms HGET/HMSET spans with sub-ms cartservice handler self-time. That would mean the delay is not in the container's namespace (e.g. it is in redis-cart itself or re-attached by the recurring platform-automation cycle), and the sidecar/automation must be addressed outside this system.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this is a pure availability cost with no benefit: in-flight cart RPCs fail during the recreate and in-process cache state is discarded. It is irreversible as an action, and if platform-automation re-attaches shaping on its 4-5h cycle the relief is temporary and may mask the real trigger.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice's inbound callers: frontend and checkoutservice see connection resets for the recreate duration, which loadgenerator will register as a brief error spike; user cart contents held only in process memory are lost.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services alerting within seconds along the cart-checkout-frontend path suggests a shared downstream failure rather than an isolated warning. With no open incidents to fold this into, it warrants investigation starting from cartservice as the earliest signal.
